items.title: 香港支聯會「煽動顛覆」案：李卓人、鄒幸彤、何俊仁判囚5至7年

items.desc: 25年後回望，這場襲擊已塑造了整整一代的外交、安全及情報政策。BBC安全事務記者如此寫道。

items.title: 「無時無刻都在想」：911事件25年後審訊仍未了，難屬傷痛難癒

items.desc: 2001年的襲擊造成數千名美國人喪生，並對全球產生了深遠影響。

items.title: 青島北海造船廠外籍貨輪大火 失聯25人已確定全部死亡
items.desc: 中國官方媒體稱，一艘外籍貨輪靠港維修期間起火，造成嚴重傷亡。習近平與李強下達救災指示。

items.title: 特朗普真的能向每位美國成年人發放5000美元嗎？
items.desc: 分析人士質疑，美國總統在選舉年提出的這項承諾，是否可行、合法且負擔得起。

items.desc: 香港記者協會主席鄭嘉如指控《華爾街日報》出版商道瓊斯，因其參與工會活動，而將其革職，法庭部分支持其主張。

items.title: AI「性轉」視頻風靡中國網絡：一場「 新文化運動」的覺醒與侷限
items.desc: 經典的「好太太」系列廣告以「好丈夫」的形象重出江湖：鏡頭前穿著清涼的不再是女性,而是男性。

items.title: 推崇⽑澤東的「Z世代」：彈幕、「教員」與政治失語
items.desc: 從2019年開始，《毛澤東選集》突然躍居清華大學圖書館年度借閱榜榜首，此後一直到2025年都穩居榜首。網絡上，不少年輕人稱毛澤東為「教員」，並追捧他的影視形象。為何這位已故領導人重新受到關注？

items.title: 2026台灣地方選舉：「九合一」為何重要？選舉時程是什麼？
items.desc: 台灣的地方選舉又稱「九合一」選舉，每四年一次，多數落在總統任期中段的年底，故被視為總統的「期中考」。

items.title: 尼泊爾給水力發電押下重注，泥石流把問題徹底暴露

items.title: 尼泊爾—西藏泥石流：堰塞湖和冰湖是下一個「定時炸彈」？

items.desc: 吉隆口岸位處西藏與尼泊爾的重要貿易通路之上，中國與尼泊爾兩側各有數以百計外國旅客在泥石流衝擊後下落不明。

items.title: 中國審查西藏口岸遭洪災衝擊畫面，當地災民情況我們所知甚少
items.desc: 一些關於這場致命山洪暴發最驚人的畫面，中國官方媒體未對公眾播放。

items.title: 專訪鄧燕娥：與李卓人相伴四十年「互相撐著」

items.title: 為甚麼Gen Z的測試成績正在下跌？
items.desc: 在全球最大的15歲青少年國際測試中，閱讀、數學和科學成績都正在下跌。這一下跌趨勢大約始於2012年，而且似乎正在加速，尤其是閱讀能力。本影片探討導致這一下跌的各種可能原因。

items.title: 「教員萬歲」：中國Z世代為何重新「擁抱」毛澤東？
items.desc: 分析認為，面對就業壓力和貧富差距，一些中國年輕人重新從毛澤東的階級論述尋找答案；毛時代強調的「獨立自主、自力更生」，在今日中西方競爭的背景下，也再次產生吸引力。

items.title: 美軍航母全數撤離印太：台灣該擔心「空窗期」嗎？

items.desc: President Putin arrived as talks among leaders of the BRICS diplomatic bloc began on Friday in India, amid global geopolitical turmoil, including the war in Ukraine and the conflict in the Middle East.

items.title: Trump will meet with Ireland's leaders before heading to his golf club in Doonbeg
items.desc: President Donald Trump arrived Saturday in Dublin, where he'll hold talks with Ireland's president and prime minister, kicking off a weekend visit that's more about a major golf tournament held on a course he owns on the country's Atlantic coast.

items.title: Céline Dion fever grips Paris ahead of sold
items.desc:
It's Céline Dion fever in Paris. She returns to the stage this Saturday, opening a sold-out Paris residency.

It will be the first of 26 concerts over the next eight months. She is making a comeback after a battle with a neurological disorder that has sidelined her career.

On the eve of her first performance, there was a giant free karaoke singalong here in the French capital to get things going.

items.title: Rennes beat Olympique de Marseille to seize top spot in Ligue 1
items.desc: It’s the same old story for Olympique de Marseille, who have now lost three matches in a row in the French championship. Struggling in every area of the pitch and lacking ideas, the Marseille side have won just one of their last four matches.

items.title: Jewish ‘supercop’ runs on Arab ticket in Israeli polls
items.desc: Former Israeli police officer Yoav Segalovitz's decision to run as the No. 2 candidate on the Arab Raam party ticket in the October 2026 elections marks a paradigm change in Israeli politics. Far-right politicians have slammed the move, but it could pave the way for an Arab party to join a coalition opposing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his allies.

items.title: Swiss researchers use AI to detect early warning signs of natural disasters
items.desc: Scientists have long warned of more intense extreme weather events in the decades to come due to our fast-warming climate. The question they are asking is how we are going to be better prepared as we become more prone to natural disasters.A group of researchers in Switzerland believe that artificial intelligence modeling could revolutionise forecasting systems.

items.title: Zelensky open to meet Putin at Miami G20 if Russian leader attends
items.desc: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said he was willing to meet Russian leader Vladimir Putin at the G20 summit in Miami. However, the Kremlin has not confirmed whether Putin would attend, and it demanded that Zelensky come to Russia for talks instead.

items.title: French police suspect Normandy train derailment was result of sabotage
items.desc: A police source said Saturday that French investigators suspect sabotage caused a train derailment in northwest France after a fragment of rail was found on the track. At least 44 people were injured in the derailment that occurred a day earlier, including an 18-year-old woman "in a critical condition".

items.title: Trump says unified Ireland ‘would be fantastic' during Dublin trip
items.desc: US President Donald Trump on Saturday said a unified Ireland would be “fantastic" during a weekend visit to a major tournament at his Irish golf course. The two-day trip to Ireland is the latest example of how the US leader blends his official duties with his personal interests.

items.title: BRICS leaders call for 'maximum restraint' as Middle East war threatens unity
items.desc: BRICS leaders meeting in New Delhi on Saturday unanimously adopted a joint declaration expressing "deep concern" over the war in the Middle East and urging maximum restraint. The statement was seen as indirect criticism of US and Israeli strikes on Iranian nuclear facilities.

items.title: Céline Dion poised for emotional comeback concert in Paris
items.desc: Céline Dion is set to return to the stage in Paris on Saturday for her first full concert in six years, capping a years-long battle with a rare autoimmune disorder and marking a major milestone in the Canadian superstar’s comeback.

items.title: Middle East live: Saudi Arabia shuts down critical oil pipeline after attacks
items.desc: Saudi Arabia on Saturday said that it has shut down its East-West pipeline as a precaution after multiple attacks on the vital oil conduit earlier this week. Both Baghdad and Riyadh said the attacks originated in Iraqi territory, where Iranian-backed militias operate. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.

items.title: Battle over 'pervert' AI glasses in Europe's line of sight after scandal
items.desc: A scandal involving girls and women filmed secretly by "pervert"  AI glasses has sparked growing concern over this emerging technology – with a petition in Britain demanding a ban on their sale. Anyone wearing smart glasses can take photos, film videos or interact with an AI assistant, with sales now hitting the millions.
